mainTopic: An אפוטרופוס for the ox of יתומים or of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, and רבי יעקב's ruling of half damages
overview: This amud opens with the end of an argument about who pays when an orphans' מועד ox does damage. One view says the orphans' property pays, so people will not refuse to be an אפוטרופוס. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says the אפוטרופוס pays and is repaid when the יתומים grow up. The גמרא then shows that appointing an אפוטרופוס for a תם ox, so damages can be collected from its body, is a dispute between סומכוס and חכמים in a ברייתא. It also explains that סומכוס and רבי יוסי argue about whether a change of רשות changes the ox's status. Next comes a ברייתא where רבי יעקב rules that half damages are paid when the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן gores. רבא explains this as a מועד given only a lesser guarding, built on two rules of רבי יהודה plus the view of the רבנן about appointing an אפוטרופוס. אביי holds that רבי יעקב and רבי יהודה really disagree, and explains the case as a מועד that was not guarded at all. The amud ends with רב אחא בר אביי asking why, according to רבא, the case was not simply set in a תם ox, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: People would refuse to become stewards
steps.stepSummary: The end of the first opinion's reasoning: if the אפוטרופוס had to pay, people would refuse the job.
steps.simpleTranslation: People would hold back and not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the reasoning of the first opinion, which was stated just before this section. That opinion holds that the damages are paid from the orphans' own property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is practical. If the אפוטרופוס had to pay out of his own pocket, nobody would agree to take care of יתומים' property. So the payment must come from the יתומים' property.

keyTerms.meaning: they hold back, refrain
and they would not do it

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an argument that started before this section. Read it as the reason for the earlier opinion, not as a new ruling.

phrases.english: they would refrain and not do it.
phrases.notes: He means: people would refuse to serve as an אפוטרופוס if they might have to pay from their own money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of the opinion stated just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment cannot come from the אפוטרופוס, or people would refuse to serve.

steps.title: The steward pays and is repaid later
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says the damages are collected from the best property of the אפוטרופוס, who is repaid by the orphans when they grow up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says: payment comes from the best-quality property of the steward, and the stewards later collect it back from the orphans when they grow up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא gives the opposite view. The אפוטרופוס pays the damages himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He answers the worry from Step 1. The אפוטרופוס does not actually lose any money, because he collects it back from the יתומים once they are adults. So people will not refuse to serve.

keyTerms.meaning: the best-quality property (עידית)
a steward or guardian appointed over someone's property
they collect repayment
orphans

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on who pays when an orphans' ox does damage. The first says the orphans' property pays, so stewards will not be scared off. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says the steward pays and is repaid when the orphans grow up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina says:
from the best-quality property of the steward,
and they then go back and collect from the orphans
when they grow up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion and removes its worry about losing stewards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damages are collected from the steward's best property, and he is repaid by the orphans later.

steps.title: Appointing stewards for a תם ox is a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that whether בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס for a תם ox, so damages can be collected from its body, is a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the statement 'we appoint stewards for them for a תם ox, to collect from its body' is a matter of dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes an earlier statement about appointing stewards for a תם ox and says that תנאים disagree about it. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תם ox pays only from its own body, meaning the money from selling it. The question is whether בית דין steps in and appoints a steward when the owners cannot act. The גמרא is saying this is not agreed on by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: appoint, set up
an ox not yet known as a habitual gorer, which pays only from its own body
from its body, meaning from the value of the ox itself
it is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: And 'we appoint stewards for them'
for a tam ox, to collect from its body,
is a dispute of Tannaim,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who pays to a related question: whether stewards are appointed for a תם ox at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Appointing stewards for a תם ox to collect from its body is a dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: ברייתא: ox whose owner is unavailable
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס says an ox whose owner is a חרש, a שוטה, or overseas stays תם. חכמים say בית דין appoints stewards and the warnings are given in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: An ox whose owner became a חרש, or became a שוטה, or went overseas. יהודה בן נקוסא said in the name of סומכוס: it stays תם until warnings are testified in front of the owner. The חכמים say: we appoint stewards for them, and testify in front of the stewards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show the dispute between תנאים it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make an ox מועד, witnesses must testify about its goring in front of the owner. At first glance סומכוס seems to say that without the real owner present, the ox can never become מועד. Steps 6 and 7 show this is not what he means. חכמים say a steward can stand in for the owner, so the ox can become מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: who became a חרש (deaf-mute)
who became a שוטה (mentally incompetent)
overseas, far away
its status of being תם
that they testify about it, which is what makes an ox מועד

phrases.english: As it is taught: An ox whose owner became a deaf-mute,
or whose owner became mentally incompetent,
or whose owner went overseas,
Yehuda ben Nekosa said in the name of Sumakhos:
it stays in its tam status
until they testify about it in front of the owner.
And the Sages say: We appoint stewards for them,
and testify about them in front of the stewards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that proves the dispute between תנאים claimed in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that appointing stewards is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: סומכוס says no stewards are appointed and the ox stays תם, while חכמים say stewards are appointed and testimony is given before them.

steps.title: When the owner becomes available again
steps.stepSummary: Once the owner recovers, grows up, or returns, סומכוס says the ox goes back to being תם. רבי יוסי says it keeps the status it already has.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the חרש regained his hearing, the שוטה became sane, the minor grew up, or the owner came back from overseas, יהודה בן נקוסא said in the name of סומכוס: it returns to being תם, until warnings are testified in front of the owner. רבי יוסי said: it stays in its established status.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to a second case. An ox was made מועד in front of stewards, and then the real owner became available again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס holds that the ox goes back to being תם, so the owner himself must be warned again. רבי יוסי says the ox stays מועד, because the warnings given in front of the stewards still count.

keyTerms.meaning: became able to hear again
became sane again
the minor reached adulthood
in its established status, here meaning it stays מועד

steps.whatToRemember: There are two disputes in this ברייתא. First, can stewards stand in for an unavailable owner so the ox becomes מועד? חכמים say yes and סומכוס says no. Second, after the owner returns, does that מועד status last? רבי יוסי says yes, while סומכוס says the ox goes back to being תם.
steps.confusionAlert: סומכוס's 'it returns to being תם' only makes sense if the ox had already become מועד while the owner was unavailable. The גמרא uses exactly this point in step 6 to show that even סומכוס agrees the ox can become מועד.

phrases.english: If the deaf-mute regained his hearing,
the mentally incompetent one became sane, or the minor grew up,
or its owner came back from overseas,
Yehuda ben Nekosa said in the name of Sumakhos:
it has returned to its tam status,
until they testify about it in front of the owner.
Rabbi Yosei said:
it remains in its established status.
phrases.notes: It stays מועד, the status it got while the stewards were in charge.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְפַּקֵּחַ הַחֵרֵשׁ, נִשְׁתַּפָּה הַשּׁוֹטֶה וְהִגְדִּיל הַקָּטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a follow-up case about the owner becoming available again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סומכוס says the ox returns to being תם once the owner is available. רבי יוסי says it keeps its מועד status.

steps.title: What did סומכוס mean by 'it stays תם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what סומכוס meant. It rejects the simple reading that the ox can never become a מועד, because the end of the ברייתא says it 'goes back' to being תם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What did סומכוס mean by 'it stays in its תמות'? If you say it never becomes a מועד at all, that can't be right. The end of the ברייתא says 'it goes back to its תמות,' which shows that it did become a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what סומכוס's words really mean. It knocks out the obvious answer so it can offer a better one in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ox never became a מועד, it could not 'go back' to being תם later. Since the end of the ברייתא (step 5) says it goes back, the ox must have become a מועד in between. So 'stays תם' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of being a תם, an ox that has not yet been warned about goring
Becomes a מועד, an ox warned about repeated goring
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
By implication; this shows that

steps.confusionAlert: In step 4 it sounded like סומכוס meant the ox can never become a מועד. The גמרא is showing that this simple reading cannot be right.

phrases.english: They said: What is 'it stays in its innocent status'
that סומכוס said?
If you say it does not become forewarned at all —
but since the last part teaches 'it goes back to its innocent status,'
phrases.notes: This is סומכוס's own line from step 5, about when the owner recovers, grows up, or returns.

phrases.english: that implies it did become forewarned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at סומכוס's words from step 4 and uses the end of the ברייתא (step 5) to rule out the simple reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does סומכוס mean by 'הרי הוא בתמותו'?

steps.title: סומכוס means the ox stays whole, so nothing is collected from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads 'בתמותו' as 'בתמימותו': the ox stays whole, and we do not take damages from it. So סומכוס holds that no אפוטרופוס is appointed to collect from a תם's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'it stays in its תמות' mean? It means it stays in its wholeness. We do not take anything away from it. So we see that we do not appoint an אפוטרופוס for a תם in order to collect from its body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of סומכוס's words. 'It stays תם' means 'it stays whole,' so no damages are taken out of the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תם's damages can only be paid from its own body. If nobody is appointed to stand in for the owner, the injured person cannot collect from the ox now. That is exactly the first side of the תנאים dispute mentioned in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Wholeness, being complete
We take away from it, we reduce it
So we see; this shows that
To collect payment from the ox's own body

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'it stays in its innocent status' mean?
It stays in its wholeness,
phrases.notes: A play on words: תמות (being a תם) and תמימות (being whole) come from the same root.

phrases.english: meaning we do not take anything away from it.
So we see: we do not appoint a steward
for an innocent ox in order to collect from its body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a new reading of סומכוס's words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בתמותו means בתמימותו: the ox stays whole and is not reduced, so no אפוטרופוס is appointed to collect from a תם.

steps.title: חכמים hold that an אפוטרופוס is appointed to collect from a תם
steps.stepSummary: Since חכמים say an אפוטרופוס is appointed and the warnings are given in front of him, they hold that one is appointed even to collect from a תם's body. This completes the proof of the תנאים dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: We appoint an אפוטרופוס for them, and the warnings are given in front of the אפוטרופוס. So we see they hold that an אפוטרופוס is appointed for a תם to collect from its body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the חכמים's side the same way. This finishes showing that the question from step 3 really is an argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there is an אפוטרופוס, he stands in for the owner. The injured person can then collect from the תם's body right away instead of waiting. סומכוס says no, חכמים say yes, and that is the dispute promised in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: They appoint
They give the formal warning in front of witnesses, which makes the ox a מועד

steps.whatToRemember: סומכוס: no אפוטרופוס for a תם, so the injured person must wait. חכמים: an אפוטרופוס is appointed, and damages can be collected from the ox's body now.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: we appoint a steward for them,
and we give the warnings in front of the steward —
so we see: we appoint a steward
for an innocent ox in order to collect from its body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading begun in step 7 by showing the חכמים take the opposite view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether an אפוטרופוס is appointed to collect from a תם's body is indeed a dispute: סומכוס says no, חכמים say yes.

steps.title: What is the argument in the last part of the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle סומכוס and רבי יוסי argue about when the owner recovers, grows up, or returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the last part of the ברייתא, what are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last part of the ברייתא from step 5 and asks what the argument there is really about. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now understand the first part of the ברייתא. But why would the ox go back to being תם (סומכוס) or keep its status (רבי יוסי)? The גמרא wants the principle behind each side.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they arguing about?

phrases.english: And in the last part, what are they arguing about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the first part of the ברייתא to its last part (step 5).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle underlies the dispute between סומכוס and רבי יוסי once the owner becomes able to take charge again?

steps.title: Does a change of custody change the ox's status?
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס holds that a change of רשות changes the ox's status. רבי יוסי holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is whether a change of רשות makes a difference. סומכוס holds that a change of רשות changes the status. רבי יוסי holds that a change of רשות does not change it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is about whether a new person in charge of the ox resets its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox became a מועד while the אפוטרופוס was in charge. When the owner takes it back, that is a change of רשות. For סומכוס this resets the ox to תם. For רבי יוסי the status belongs to the ox itself, so it stays a מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Custody; who is in charge of the ox
Changes, makes a difference
Between them

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'רשות משנה' is a general principle about whether a מועד status belongs to the animal or depends on who owns it.

phrases.english: Whether a change of custody makes a difference is between them —
phrases.notes: Here 'custody' means the ox moves from the steward back to the owner.

phrases.english: סומכוס holds: custody changes the status,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: רְשׁוּת אֵינָהּ מְשַׁנָּה.
phrases.english: and רבי יוסי holds: custody does not change it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about רשות משנה: סומכוס says a change of custody resets the status, רבי יוסי says it does not.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: half damages for the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: when an ox belonging to a חרש, שוטה, or קטן gores, רבי יעקב holds that half damages are paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: An ox of a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן that gored: רבי יעקב says half damages are paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about an ox owned by someone who cannot be held responsible. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually these owners are not held liable. Here רבי יעקב rules that half damages are paid even so. The גמרא will go on to ask what kind of ox this is, and רבא will explain it as a מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
Half damages, the payment for a תם ox

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שׁוֹר חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁנָּגַח –
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: An ox of a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor that gored —
רבי יעקב: pays half damages.
phrases.notes: This doesn't mean רבי יעקב pays out of his own pocket. It means that, in his view, half damages are paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שׁוֹר חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁנָּגַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on the related topic of oxen owned by those who cannot be held responsible.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יעקב, half damages are paid when the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן gores.

steps.title: Why would רבי יעקב himself be paying?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's wording sounds as if רבי יעקב personally pays, and the גמרא asks what he has to do with this ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רבי יעקב have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with how the ברייתא is worded. It sounds as if רבי יעקב himself is the one paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב is not the owner of the ox, and he is not its guardian. So the wording cannot mean that he personally pays, and something in the text must be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his connection? What does he have to do with it?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov — what is his business here?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's wording read like "רבי יעקב pays," as if he himself had to pay for the ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrasing of the ברייתא that seems to make רבי יעקב the payer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יעקב has no link to the ox, so he cannot be the one who pays.

steps.title: Read it as רבי יעקב saying that half is paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: רבי יעקב is stating a ruling that the ox's damages are half paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: רבי יעקב says that half damages are paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא. רבי יעקב is giving a ruling, not paying himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the word 'אומר' turns the line into a legal opinion. The opinion is that half damages are paid for this ox. Now the question becomes why the answer is exactly half.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say this instead; the wording is being corrected
Half the damages

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Rabbi Yaakov says:
he pays half damages.
phrases.notes: "He" means the payment owed for this ox, not רבי יעקב himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יעקב rules that half damages are paid

steps.title: Half damages fits neither a תם nor a מועד
steps.stepSummary: If the ox is a תם, half damages is obvious. If it is a מועד, the owner should pay either nothing or full damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If it is a תם, that is obvious, since everyone agrees a תם pays half damages. If it is a מועד: if it was guarded, nothing should be paid at all; if it was not guarded, full damages should be paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יעקב's ruling. It tries every type of ox and finds that 'half damages' does not seem to fit any of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a תם, everyone already agrees that half is paid, so רבי יעקב would be teaching nothing new. For a מועד, the law seems to be all or nothing. Guarding it means no payment, and not guarding it means full payment. So where would 'half' come from?

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
An ox that has not yet been established as a gorer; it pays half damages
A forewarned ox, established as a gorer; it pays full damages
It is obvious, so why say it?
Guarding the animal

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If with a תם, it is obvious,
since according to everyone as well
it is half damages that he pays!
And if with a מועד,
if they guarded it,
phrases.notes: "They" means whoever is in charge of the ox for the חרש, שוטה, or קטן.

phrases.english: he should not have to pay anything at all,
and if they did not guard it,
he should have to pay full damages!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the wording is fixed, the גמרא challenges the content of the ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יעקב's ruling of half damages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every possible case gives either an obvious answer (תם) or a result of nothing or full (מועד), never a new teaching of half.

steps.title: רבא: a מועד that was guarded only with a lesser guarding
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the case is a מועד that was given a lesser guarding but not a superior guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really it is a מועד. Here we are dealing with a case where they guarded it with a lesser guarding, but did not give it a superior guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He picks a middle case between 'guarded' and 'not guarded'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that an ox is either guarded or not guarded. רבא points out a third case: a lesser guarding that is good enough in some ways but not in others. That middle level of guarding is what can produce exactly half damages.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; we keep the original option
A lesser, basic guarding
A superior, extra-careful guarding

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the lesser guarding alone produces 'half'. The half comes from combining this guarding with רבי יהודה's view that a מועד keeps its תם part. The next step explains this.

phrases.english: Rava said: Actually it is about a מועד,
and here, what are we dealing with?
where they gave it a lesser guarding,
and did not give it a superior guarding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by finding a middle case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מועד is either guarded (pay nothing) or not guarded (pay full)
steps.terutzMaskana: A מועד given only a lesser guarding is a middle case

steps.title: רבי יעקב follows two views of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב holds like רבי יהודה that the תם part of a מועד stays in place, and also like רבי יהודה that a lesser guarding is enough for a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יעקב holds like רבי יהודה, who says the תם part stays in its place. And he also holds like רבי יהודה, who says a lesser guarding is enough for a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's answer. It shows how the lesser guarding leads to exactly half damages, by pointing to two rulings of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First rule: even a מועד keeps its old 'תם half', so it pays two halves, one as a תם and one as a מועד. Second rule: for the מועד half, a lesser guarding is enough, so that half is not owed. The תם half still needs a superior guarding, which was not given, so that half is paid. The result is exactly half damages.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'תם side' of the ox stays in its place even after it becomes a מועד
It is enough for it

steps.whatToRemember: Half damages = the תם half (lesser guarding is not enough for it, so it is paid) + the מועד half (lesser guarding is enough, so it is not paid). This only works if you hold both of רבי יהודה's rules.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how two separate rules can combine to produce a new result. That is why רבי יעקב's ruling is not obvious after all.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה –
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: the element of being a תם stays in its place;
phrases.notes: A מועד still pays half of its damages as a תם, and only the other half as a מועד.

phrases.english: and he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: מוּעָד סַגִּי לֵיהּ בִּשְׁמִירָה פְּחוּתָה;
phrases.english: who says: for a מועד, a lesser guarding is enough;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by giving the principles that turn a lesser guarding into half damages.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Basing the ruling on two known opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lesser guarding cannot explain why exactly half would be paid
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי יהודה twice, the תם half is paid and the מועד half is excused

steps.title: רבא's third point: a guardian is appointed for a תם
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that רבי יעקב also holds like the רבנן: the court appoints an אפוטרופוס for the owner of a תם, so the half damages can be collected from the ox itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he holds like the רבנן, who say: we appoint a guardian for a תם so the damages can be collected from its body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation of רבי יעקב with one more opinion that רבי יעקב agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 explained why the damages are half: the תם part stays, and a lesser guarding is enough. That still leaves a question, because the owner is a חרש, שוטה or קטן, so who pays? רבא's answer is that the court appoints a guardian, and the half damages are collected from the ox's body.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
A guardian appointed to manage the affairs of someone who cannot manage them himself
To collect from its body, meaning from the ox itself

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי יעקב's ruling rests on three opinions. The תם part of a מועד stays (רבי יהודה). A lesser guarding is enough for a מועד (רבי יהודה). A guardian is appointed to collect from the ox's body (רבנן).

phrases.english: And he holds like the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יעקב. רבא is still explaining his ruling.

phrases.english: who say: we appoint a guardian for a tam
phrases.notes: He means the owner of the ox is someone who can't manage his own affairs, so the court appoints someone to act for him.

phrases.english: to collect from its body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation from step 16 by adding a third opinion that רבי יעקב follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a further legal assumption that explains how the payment is collected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the owner is a חרש, שוטה or קטן, maybe nothing can be collected at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A guardian is appointed, and the half damages are collected from the ox's body.

steps.title: אביי asks: don't רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב disagree?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא by quoting a ברייתא where רבי יהודה obligates the owner and רבי יעקב says only half damages are paid. That sounds like an argument, not agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do they not disagree? But it was taught: an ox of a חרש, a שוטה or a קטן that gored, רבי יהודה obligates, and רבי יעקב says he pays half damages.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רבא's claim that רבי יעקב simply follows רבי יהודה. He brings a ברייתא where the two seem to argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that רבי יעקב holds like רבי יהודה. In this ברייתא, רבי יהודה obligates the owner and רבי יעקב says only half, which looks like two different rulings. If they argue, then רבי יעקב cannot be following רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they don't disagree? (said as a challenge)
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
Holds him liable

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And do they not disagree?!
But it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל חֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁנָּגַח –
phrases.english: An ox of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor that gored:
Rabbi Yehuda obligates,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: חֲצִי נֶזֶק הוּא דִּמְשַׁלֵּם!
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yaakov says: it is half damages that he pays!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's claim from steps 16 and 17 that רבי יעקב follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that רבי יעקב holds like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows the two giving different rulings, so רבי יעקב cannot simply be following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: רבי יעקב is only explaining רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא answers that there is no argument in that ברייתא. רבי יעקב is explaining how much רבי יהודה obligates: half damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: What רבי יהודה obligates, רבי יעקב explained.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to אביי's challenge: the two תנאים are not arguing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said only "he is obligated" and did not say how much. רבי יעקב fills in the amount: half damages. So the ברייתא is not a dispute, and רבא's claim that רבי יעקב follows רבי יהודה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Explained

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי יעקב's "half damages" as disagreeing with רבי יהודה. In this reading, he is only giving the amount that רבי יהודה left out.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
What Rabbi Yehuda obligates,
Rabbi Yaakov explained.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: מַה שֶּׁמְּחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פֵּירֵשׁ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by rereading the ברייתא as an explanation instead of a dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא so that the second opinion explains the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב are arguing about how much is paid.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יעקב is only spelling out the amount that רבי יהודה obligates.

steps.title: According to אביי, what is their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: אביי holds that רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב do disagree, so what is their disagreement about?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, who says they disagree, what do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step. It asks how אביי would describe the dispute, since he believes there is one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי rejected the idea that the two תנאים agree. If they argue, the case must be one where their rulings really differ. The גמרא wants to know what that case is.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, who says they disagree,
about what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רבא to explaining אביי's own reading of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case would make רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב really disagree, according to אביי

steps.title: אביי: the case is a מועד that was not guarded at all
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, the ברייתא is talking about a מועד ox that was not guarded at all. רבי יהודה obligates, and רבי יעקב says only half damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: Here we are dealing with a מועד that was not guarded at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for אביי by setting the case as a מועד ox with no guarding at all. This is a different case from רבא's, which had a lesser guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case had a מועד with a lesser guarding, where both תנאים can agree on half damages. אביי moves the case to a מועד that was not guarded at all. In that case רבי יהודה obligates the owner, while רבי יעקב still says only half, so they really disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with?
An ox with an established pattern of goring
And did not guard it at all

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: a מועד with a lesser guarding, and the תנאים agree. אביי: a מועד with no guarding at all, and the תנאים disagree.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
phrases.notes: "He" is אביי. The גמרא is answering on his behalf.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With a muad, and it was not guarded at all.
phrases.notes: Compare step 15: there רבא's case had a lesser guarding. Here there was no guarding at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by defining the case as one where the Tannaim's rulings differ.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about a מועד that was not guarded at all.

steps.title: Where רבי יעקב agrees with רבי יהודה and where he disagrees
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, רבי יעקב agrees with רבי יהודה that a מועד ox still keeps its 'תם part'. He disagrees about appointing an אפוטרופוס to collect that תם half from the ox's body, so in his view only the מועד half is paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and argues with him on one point. He agrees that when an ox becomes מועד, its תם part stays in place, so the damages are made of two halves. He argues about whether the court appoints an אפוטרופוס for a תם so that payment can be taken from the ox's body. רבי יהודה says the court does appoint one. רבי יעקב says it does not, so only the מועד half gets paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing אביי's answer from the last step. It explains exactly what רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב agree on and what they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a מועד ox's full damages split into two halves: a 'תם half' and an extra 'מועד half'. The argument is only about the תם half, which is collected from the ox's own body. רבי יהודה says the court appoints an אפוטרופוס so that half can be collected. רבי יעקב says no, so the תם half is lost and only the מועד half is paid.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'תם part' of the ox. The half-damages part that stays even after the ox becomes מועד
Stays in its place. It is still there and was not erased
A guardian or manager the court appoints to handle someone's property
To collect from its body, meaning from the ox itself
The מועד half. The extra half that a מועד ox's owner pays

steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's view, רבי יעקב agrees that a מועד ox has a תם part. He only disagrees about appointing an אפוטרופוס to collect it. That is why he says only half damages are paid.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'half damages' does not mean the ox is just a תם. The ox is מועד. The half that gets paid is the מועד half, because the תם half cannot be collected without an אפוטרופוס.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov agrees with Rabbi Yehuda on one point,
and argues with him on one point.
He agrees with Rabbi Yehuda on one point:
for Rabbi Yehuda holds:
the 'innocent part' stays in its place;
phrases.notes: Even after the ox becomes מועד, its first half-damages, the תם part, is still there. רבי יעקב agrees with this.

phrases.english: and he argues with him on one point:
for Rabbi Yehuda holds:
they appoint a guardian for them for an innocent ox
to collect from its body,
and Rabbi Yaakov holds: they do not appoint one,
and he pays only the half of the forewarned part.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 21 by explaining what the disagreement is about
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both agree a מועד ox keeps its תם part. They argue only about whether an אפוטרופוס is appointed to collect the תם half from the ox's body. רבי יעקב says no, so only the מועד half is paid.

steps.title: Why not set the case in a תם ox according to רבא?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אביי says to רבינא: אביי's reading works because he holds that the two argue. But רבא holds they do not argue, so the case should have been set in a תם ox instead of a מועד ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אביי said to רבינא: For אביי, who says the two argue, everything works out well. But for רבא, who says they do not argue, why set the case in a מועד ox? Set it in a תם ox instead!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רב אחא בר אביי asks רבינא how the מועד setup fits רבא's view that there is no argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מועד case was built to create a real argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב, which fits אביי. רבא says they do not argue at all. For him, it seems simpler to set the case in a תם ox, where 'half damages' just explains רבי יהודה. So why bring in a מועד ox at all?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted. This opens 'this view works, but the other one is hard'
Fine, it works out well
Instead of setting it (the case) in
Let him set it (the case) in

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּיֵי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Abaye said to Ravina:
Granted, according to Abaye, who says they argue, it is fine;
but according to Rava, who says they do not argue,
instead of setting it in a forewarned ox,
let him set it in an innocent ox!
phrases.notes: With a תם ox, 'half damages' would simply explain רבי יהודה's ruling, with no argument needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַבָּיֵי דְּאָמַר פְּלִיגִי – שַׁפִּיר; אֶלָּא לְרָבָא דְּאָמַר לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's מועד setup and asks how a מועד setting fits רבא's no-argument view
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב do not argue
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מועד setting fits a view that has a real argument. For רבא, with no argument, a תם setting seems more natural, so why use a מועד ox?
